services.notes: VulnHub Mr-Robot:1 writeup consensus (e.g. christophetd, abatchy, common walkthroughs): HTTP landing page; robots.txt exposes /fsocity.dic (large custom wordlist, many duplicates) and /key-1-of-3.txt (flag1). WordPress CMS with /wp-login.php and /wp-admin/; readme.html indicates WordPress ~4.3.x; theme twentyfifteen often observed. Nikto/dirb typically surface wp-login and WordPress paths. Login form distinguishes invalid username vs bad password (useful for username then password enumeration with fsocity.dic). Documented CTF chain often finds WP user 'elliot'. XML-RPC may be enabled. No claim that credentials are present in this JSON as live secrets—treat as lab training evidence aligned with public writeups.

scenario_objective: Authorized LADE lab: draft and attempt plausible paths toward MrRobot flags / root using neuro-symbolic AutoPlan-RT under human lab policy.
attack_objective: Obtain progressive access on VulnHub Mr-Robot:1 (web recon → WordPress risk → local user → privilege escalation) in the authorized cyberrange only.
security_notes: Topo LADE: kali 192.168.1.10 (Net1 + WAN) -- router -- mrrobot on Net2. Update mrrobot.ip after DHCP. Public writeup chain (training): robots/fsocity → WP login user elliot → weak WP password from wordlist → admin plugin/theme code exec (e.g. exploit/unix/webapp/wp_admin_shell_upload) → local user robot with MD5 password.raw-md5 crackable → SUID nmap 3.81 interactive (!sh) for root. Do not use outside authorized lab.

pistes_documentees.synthese: fsocity.dic wordlist + key-1-of-3.txt on webroot; first flag often trivial via robots.
Enumerate WP user (elliot common in writeups) then password via fsocity.dic; authenticated admin can upload plugin or use theme editor; MSF wp_admin_shell_upload documented in public walkthroughs.
After user robot: /usr/local/bin/nmap SUID old interactive mode allows !command as root (writeup consensus).

network_policies.description: Router forwards Kali (Net1) to MrRobot (Net2); WAN on Net1 for LLM API only.
